title: Startups in Underdog Cities
primary_theme: Investing in founders and companies outside the traditional startup hubs
founder_lessons: There are great founders and companies outside Silicon Valley; invest where there is less competition and more opportunity.
Founders prefer capital from people who have walked in their shoes and understand the path they are on.
Being visible and responsive builds trust, especially when founders can easily reach you and your network.
A strong local community and referral network can be a differentiator for early-stage deal sourcing.
community_organizations: Apex Center for Entrepreneurship at Virginia Tech
notable_quotes: I have spent my career building companies in what I like to call underdog cities across the country.
Most founders, especially at the very early stages of a company, would prefer to raise capital from somebody that has walked in their shoes versus somebody that has not.
I make myself visible. So there should be a way for you to find someone in my network.
